newsitem.title: USA: Jesse Jackson plans hearing on job discrimination.
newsitem.headline: Jesse Jackson plans hearing on job discrimination.

text.p: Civil rights leader Jesse Jackson said Wednesday he would conduct a public hearing in Chicago on Saturday, December 7, on race and age discrimination and sexual harassment in the workplace.
In a statement, Jackson, president of Rainbow PUSH Coalition, said U.S. Assistant Secretary of Labor Bernard Anderson would oversee the hearing.

On Monday Jackson led a demonstration against Chicago-based printing company R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co, the target of a $500 million federal class-action lawsuit alleging race discrimination based on layoffs, promotions and wages.

Jackson said representatives from the U.S. Congress, U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Illinois Departmend of Human Rights and various legal and labor groups also would be on hand to hear the testimony.
The hearing, to start at 1130 CST, is scheduled for two hours following the Rainbow PUSH Saturday morning forum.
